accueil.avis.1: “The garden is beautiful in every season, and the big glass doors mean you can enjoy it even when it rains. We will be back.”
accueil.avis.2: “A quiet street that leads only to the riverbank, and yet the town centre on foot. We did not get back in the car all week.”
accueil.avis.3: “An exceptional welcome from Claire, and excellent advice on exploring the region. Everything is tastefully decorated, spotlessly clean, with good beds.”
accueil.avis.intro: 23 reviews on Google, 62 on Airbnb, and a 100 % response rate.
accueil.avis.note: Extracts translated and shortened from reviews published on Google and on Airbnb.
accueil.cta.p: For availability and prices, give your dates and the number of guests: a reply usually comes back within a few hours.
accueil.desc: Three-star gîte in Charleville-Mézières, sleeping 2 to 5. A 500 m² enclosed garden, steps from the Trans-Ardennes greenway and the Meuse, a ten-minute walk from Place Ducale. Book direct, no commission.
accueil.hero.lead: A three-star gîte, fully renovated, sleeping 2 to 5. A 10-minute walk from Place Ducale, steps from the greenway.
accueil.hero.titre: A family house opening onto 500 m² of garden, a short walk from the Meuse.
accueil.hote.p1: I work in tourism, and my guests get the benefit of it: I can point you to bike rides, walks, museums, monuments, good restaurants and country markets, in the town and across the whole département.
accueil.hote.p2: I have been welcoming guests for 9 years and I answer every enquiry, usually within a few hours. The welcome is the third most mentioned subject in the reviews, after the garden and the location.
accueil.hote.p3: Check-in is self-service, using a secure key box, between 5 pm and 8 pm. Check-out is before 11 am.
accueil.jardin.cap2: An armchair in the middle of the lawn
accueil.jardin.cap3: The squirrels are at home here
accueil.jardin.intro: It is what comes up most often in the reviews: of 62 comments, 39 mention the outdoor space before anything else. Wooded, full of flowers, completely enclosed, with a terrace on the same level as the living room. Somewhere to have breakfast outside, let the children run about, or do nothing at all.
accueil.lieu.p1: No through traffic: rue Saint-Aubin serves nothing but the houses on it, and ends in the path down to the Meuse and the greenway. That is what makes it so quiet, and it is the second most praised thing in the reviews.
accueil.lieu.p2: The neighbourhood feels like a village, with its shops and its bus stop. And the centre of Charleville — Place Ducale, its cafés, its cinema — is a 10-minute walk away.
accueil.lieu.p3: From the garden gate you join 85 km of traffic-free cycle path, from Charleville to Givet and the Belgian border.
accueil.lieu.titre: A street that leads only to the riverbank
accueil.maison.cap4: The house, seen from the garden
accueil.maison.intro: A detached house from the early twentieth century, fully renovated: 70 m², two bedrooms, a bathroom, a fitted kitchen and a fireplace. The living room opens straight onto the terrace through large glass doors.
accueil.maison.savoir.p: the stairs are steep, and the bathroom is reached through the first-floor bedroom. Not an issue for a family; worth bearing in mind between adults who do not know each other.
accueil.maison.savoir.t: Two things to know before you book:

contact.titre: Contact and getting here — Gîte Saint-Aubin, Charleville-Mézières
contact.venir.p1: By train: Charleville-Mézières station is 5 minutes away by car, and the number 7 bus stops just along the road. Paris is under 2 hours away.
contact.venir.p2: By bike: the Trans-Ardennes greenway runs past the end of the street. There is a bike shelter outside — do mention it in your message.
contact.venir.p3: By car: free parking alongside the property, in a street with no through traffic. The Belgian border is 30 minutes away.
contact.venir.titre: By train, by bike, or by car
eco.desc: The gîte takes part in the Interreg “Ardenne Écotourisme” programme: shower timer, water jug, zero-waste containers, recycling and compost. A renovation carried out with local craftspeople and low-carbon materials.
eco.g1.p: 5 minutes, the length of a shower. Turn it over as you step in, and see whether you can keep to it.
eco.g2.p: A sticker shows the water level that is enough. It sits low on purpose: any higher and it would encourage you to use more.
eco.g3.p: “Just water! 100 % Ardenne, 0 % waste” — the water here is meant for a glass, not a plastic bottle.
eco.g4.p: Boxes and jars, so you can take a picnic onto the greenway without single-use packaging.
eco.g5.p: Turn the heating off before airing the room: it is written on the sticker, next to the thermostat.
eco.g5.t: Heating off before the windows open
eco.g6.p: A sticker sheet shows what goes where. Peelings go to the compost heap, and come back as flower beds.
eco.g6.t: Sorting, and the compost at the bottom of the garden
eco.gestes.intro: The programme’s kit is in three languages — French, English and Dutch. Each sticker is placed in the room it refers to: bathroom, kitchen, living rooms.
eco.gestes.titre: What you will find when you arrive
eco.hero.lead: The gîte takes part in the European Interreg programme “Ardenne Écotourisme”. In practice, a few stickers around the rooms are reminders of simple things you can do for nature. Take them as a little challenge for the length of your stay.
eco.label.p1: It is an Interreg programme, run on both sides of the border with Accueil Champêtre en Wallonie, Ardennes de France and the RND Pierre + Bois network. It gives accommodation owners a signage kit and a shared framework.
eco.label.p2: The gîte is also listed in the ecotourism section of VisitArdenne.
eco.label.p3: The kit is published in French, English and Dutch — like a good share of the guests, who come from Belgium and the Netherlands.
eco.m1.p: The house was renovated by firms from the Ardennes, using natural or low-carbon materials.
eco.m2.p: Heating comes from a heat pump. The fireplace tops it up in winter.
eco.m3.p: Careful water use, a shower timer, and tap water served at the table.
eco.m6.p: The gîte is a member of the organic grocery La Marcasserie, and the country markets are gladly pointed out.
eco.maison.intro: The renovation was carried out with craftspeople from the region and low-carbon materials. These are choices you cannot see, and they matter far more than the shower timer.
eco.maison.titre: What was done before you arrived
jardin.a1.p: 85 km without a car along the Meuse, from Charleville to Givet and the Belgian border. It is also EuroVelo 19, the Meuse cycle route, which carries on down to the North Sea.
jardin.a2.p: Place Ducale is the twin sister of the Place des Vosges in Paris, built in the seventeenth century. Shops, restaurants, a cinema, the market and the tourist office.
jardin.a3.p: On the bank of the Meuse, in the old mill, devoted to Arthur Rimbaud, born in Charleville, and to his work. His birthplace and his grave are on the same walk.
jardin.a4.p: Swimming pool and spa, a small marina, a park, sports pitches and a skatepark, at the foot of Mont-Olympe.
jardin.a4.t: The water sports centre and Mont-Olympe
jardin.a5.p: Down the valley: Monthermé, the Dames de Meuse, the Rocher de l’Ermitage, and Belgium half an hour away by car.
jardin.a6.p: A village feel, with all the town’s shops and services on foot or by bike: restaurants, a cinema, a bowling alley. The number 7 bus to the station stops nearby.
jardin.autour.intro: The street leads only to the riverbank. From the garden gate you reach the Meuse and 85 km of cycle path without ever meeting a car.
jardin.cap.bateaux: Barges and boats on the Meuse
jardin.cap.port: The marina, a short ride away
jardin.cap.voieverte: The greenway in autumn, on the way out of town
jardin.desc: 500 m² of enclosed, wooded garden, terrace and barbecue, steps from the Trans-Ardennes greenway and the Meuse. Place Ducale a ten-minute walk away, the Rimbaud museum, the Mont-Olympe water sports centre.
jardin.hero.lead: It is what the reviews talk about most: 39 of the 62 comments mention the outdoor space — ahead of the location, ahead of the welcome, ahead of the house itself.
jardin.hotes.intro: This is not a figure of speech: red squirrels cross the terrace and the birds have taken over the trees. The garden also gives redcurrants and wild strawberries.
jardin.hotes.titre: A paradise for birds and squirrels
jardin.j.cap2: Hardy geraniums and the old wall, at the bottom of the garden
jardin.j.cap3: The garden seen from the far end of the plot
jardin.j.p1: Surrounded by an old stone wall and a hedge, planted with tall trees. Climbing roses, day lilies, borage, redcurrants, wild strawberries: it flowers from spring to autumn.
jardin.j.p2: The terrace is on the same level as the living room, with garden furniture and enough space that nobody is on top of anybody else.
jardin.j.p3: The garden is completely enclosed: children can play in it without being watched every minute.
jardin.saisons.cap5: The house from the garden, in October
jardin.saisons.intro: The house is open all year, and the big glass doors mean you can enjoy the garden even when it rains — one of the comments that comes back most often.
jardin.saisons.titre: It does not close in October
jardin.titre: The garden and the area — Gîte Saint-Aubin, Charleville-Mézières
maison.chambres.cap3: Second floor: two beds in place, a third on request
maison.chambres.intro: The house is laid out to welcome a family more easily than a group of friends: parents on the first floor, children on the second. That does not stop friends from booking it.
maison.cuisine.cap2: The conservatory in autumn, level with the garden
maison.cuisine.p1: Induction hob, oven, microwave, dishwasher, fridge, insulated filter coffee maker, kettle, toaster. Enough to cook for five without having to borrow anything.
maison.cuisine.p2: One wall is orange, the one beside it is ochre. This is not a beige house, and that is deliberate.
maison.desc: 70 m² fully renovated: a living room opening onto the garden, fitted kitchen, fireplace, two bedrooms, walk-in shower. Facilities, baby equipment and what to know before you book.
maison.e1.p: A heat pump, underfloor heating on the ground floor, and a fireplace in the dining area. The house is open all year.
maison.e2.p: Dishwasher, oven, microwave, induction hob, fridge, coffee maker, kettle, toaster.
maison.e3.p: Bed linen and towels provided, washing machine, iron and ironing board.
maison.e4.p: Free Wi-Fi. The station is 5 minutes away by car: the house suits work trips as well.
maison.e5.p: A terrace on the same level, garden furniture, a bike shelter, 500 m² enclosed and wooded.
maison.e6.p: Free parking alongside the property. The number 7 bus stops nearby, and the station is 5 minutes away.
maison.eq1.p: A large bedroom with a double bed, wide floorboards and an antique wardrobe. It is also the way through to the bathroom.
maison.eq2.p: A room under the eaves, with a washbasin, an arched window and a roof window. Two single beds are always made up, and a third is added on request: three sleeping places, making five people in all.
maison.eq3.p: Walk-in shower, wall-hung WC, washing machine, exposed beam. Bed linen and towels are provided, and there is an iron. A second WC, reached only from outside, is next to the bike shelter.
maison.familles.p1: The second-floor room was fitted out for children: a moon-shaped wall light, a glowing heart and coloured lights on the ceiling. Simple things, and children love them.
maison.familles.p3: Baby equipment is available, including a travel cot, and the garden is completely enclosed. There are books and games downstairs.
maison.hero.lead: A detached house from the early twentieth century, 70 m² over three levels, rated three stars. Renovated with craftspeople from the region and low-carbon materials.
maison.savoir.cap: The bathroom door, from the first-floor bedroom
maison.savoir.d1p: Both the flight to the first floor and the one to the second: narrow treads and a marked pitch, as is often the case in old houses. Anyone reasonably mobile will manage them without difficulty.
maison.savoir.d2p: It is the only way in. Not an issue for a family; worth bearing in mind if you are coming as adults who do not know each other.
maison.savoir.d2t: The bathroom is reached through the first-floor bedroom
maison.savoir.d3p: The bedrooms are spread over two upper floors, there is no lift and the bathroom is on the first floor. Only the living room, the kitchen and the terrace are at ground level.
maison.savoir.d3t: The house is not suitable for people with reduced mobility
maison.savoir.d4p: The second-floor room has its own washbasin. For the shower and the WC, everyone comes down to the first floor.
maison.savoir.d4t: A washbasin on the second floor, but only one bathroom
maison.savoir.intro: An old house has its quirks. Better to know them before you book.
maison.sdb.p1: A level walk-in shower, a wall-hung WC, a washing machine, and an exposed beam that gives away the age of the house. Towels and bed linen are provided.
maison.sdb.p2: It is on the first floor, and you reach it by walking through the bedroom. It is the only way in — better to know before you arrive.
maison.sdb.titre: A walk-in shower, under the eaves
maison.vivre.cap1: The ground floor, seen from the entrance
maison.vivre.p1: The ground floor is open from end to end: the sitting area, the dining area and the conservatory are all one space. The glass doors run down to floor level and open straight onto the terrace — you can step out barefoot for your coffee.
maison.vivre.p2: A travertine floor, a pale wood panelled wall, a fireplace, and a table that seats 6 to 8. The bookshelves are under the stairs, along with the games.
maison.vivre.titre: One large room, with the garden at the end
